title: Instrumentation at the composition root and the indexer worker

details.contract:
`src/index.ts` and `src/shared/cli/args.ts` are the only files this task changes. `src/index.ts` may import `#shared/telemetry/record` and `#shared/telemetry/telemetry`; it must not import anything from `src/tools/**` beyond the manifests and handlers it already imports, and `tests/boundary.test.ts` must stay unmodified. Phase_0's `createTelemetry`, `nullTelemetry`, `Telemetry`, `CallSpec`, `RecordStatus` and `AppConfig["telemetry"]` already exist.

**args.ts — the supplied names, additively.** `parseCliArgs` (232) reads argv into a `raw` record that holds only what the caller wrote and ends by handing it to `parseArgs` (314), which fills every declared default (200-211). Extract that reader into a private `readArgv(tool, input, argv): Record<string, unknown>` and add one export beside `parseCliArgs`:

export interface ParsedCliArgs { readonly args: ToolArgs; readonly supplied: readonly string[] }
export function parseCliArgsAndNames(tool: string, input: InputLiteral, argv: readonly string[]): ParsedCliArgs;

`supplied` is `Object.keys(raw).sort()` — the `raw` record only ever holds declared names (an unknown option is refused at 255-257), so it is exactly the declared names whose source value was not `undefined`, which is the default-free answer. Keep `parseCliArgs` exactly as it is, returning `.args`: `src/index.ts:706` and `tests/cli-args.test.ts:260-262` assert the current shape, and that test file belongs to phase_2 (TASK-017), so a return-type change here would turn this phase's green gate red for a file no phase_1 task may touch.

**The recorder is created exactly once per process, in `main`, immediately after `loadConfig`:**

const sessionMode: SessionMode = mode === "mcp" ? "mcp" : mode === "worker" || mode === "index" ? "worker" : "cli";
const telemetry = config.telemetry.enabled
  ? createTelemetry({ dir: config.telemetry.dir, repoRoot: config.repoRoot, dataDir: config.dataDir, sessionMode, serverVersion: SERVER_VERSION, graphSchemaVersion: schemaVersion() })
  : nullTelemetry();

`SERVER_VERSION` is the existing literal at line 103 and `schemaVersion()` is already imported from `#shared/store/migrate`; neither is duplicated. `createTelemetry` emits the only `session` record of the process.

1. `callTool(store, tools, params)` gains a fourth parameter `telemetry: Telemetry` and one wrapper: `const started = Date.now()`, `let envelope: Envelope<unknown> | null = null`, `let parsed: ToolArgs = {}`, `let supplied: readonly string[] = []`, `let errorCode: string | null = null` before the body; every existing `return answer(X)` becomes `envelope = X; errorCode = X.error?.code ?? null; return answer(X);`; the handler call at 474 assigns `parsed = parseArgs(...)`; the `finally` calls

const recordedTool = tools.has(params.name) ? params.name : "unknown";
telemetry.recordCall({ tool: recordedTool, args: parsed, suppliedNames: supplied, envelope, status: envelope?.status ?? "absent", errorCode, durationMs: Date.now() - started });

with `supplied = Object.keys(params.arguments ?? {}).filter((name) => Object.hasOwn(tool.input, name))` computed once after the tool lookup. Both clamps are load-bearing. The `filter` is not decoration: `parseArgs` silently drops undeclared keys (the `for (const [name, field] of Object.entries(input))` loop at `src/shared/cli/args.ts:200-218`, which only ever copies a name the manifest declares), so a client that sends `{"/home/me/secret.ts": 1}` would otherwise put a path-shaped **name** into `arg_names_set`, the one field the privacy rule lets be dynamic; an undeclared key is not an argument and does not belong in the set. `recordedTool` is clamped for the same reason: `params.name` is whatever the client sent (437-439), and on the unknown-tool branch there is no `tool` object at all, so the record says `"unknown"` rather than echoing the string. `"unknown"` is the only recorded tool name that is not one of the seven.
2. `runTool(name, argv, config)` gains a `telemetry: Telemetry` parameter and the same wrapper shape, with `parsed`/`supplied` coming from `parseCliArgsAndNames` (declared outside the try). Its `--help` path returns before any record is built and must stay record-free; the `refused` early return sets `errorCode = store.error.code` with `envelope` left null; the absent branch has two shapes (`status` writes `store.reason` and returns 0 at 726-729; every other tool writes a bootstrapping envelope and returns `EXIT_FAILURE`). The `finally` calls `telemetry.close()` because a tool invocation is a one-shot process.
3. **`status` is derived from the outcome.** A record's `status` and the process exit code can never contradict each other: envelope present ⇒ `envelope.status` (`ok`/`ambiguous`/`not_found`/`error`/`bootstrapping`); no envelope and exit 0 ⇒ `"absent"`, which is the CLI's no-graph `status` line — a successful process that produced no envelope, and `envelope?.status ?? "error"` would have recorded it as a failure; no envelope and a non-zero exit ⇒ `"error"`. The MCP surface always builds an envelope, so `"absent"` is CLI-only.
4. `Lifecycle` gains `telemetry: Telemetry | null`, and `shutdown` calls `telemetry.close()` as its last step — after the watcher, the lock and the connection — so buffered records are written once, idempotently, on SIGINT, SIGTERM and stdin EOF.
5. `runMcp(config)` becomes `runMcp(config, telemetry: Telemetry)` and seeds `lifecycle.telemetry`; `main` wraps its dispatch in `try { … } finally { if (sessionMode !== "mcp") telemetry.close(); }` so a usage refusal (unknown tool name, exit 2) still writes its session record.
6. `workerOptions(argv, config)` gains `telemetry` in its returned object, so `runWorker` receives the instance; `runWorker` builds no recorder of its own and reads no environment variable.

`budget_tokens` needs no special path: it is read from the parsed `args.budget`, which `parseArgs` has already defaulted from the manifest — the **effective** budget. The supplied-name set is the only default-free field, because recording the defaulted names would make `arg_names_set` a constant of the schema instead of a fact about the caller.

Do not change any rendered output, any exit code, any manifest, or any envelope field.
details.goal: Every tool call from either surface — MCP or CLI — produces exactly one `call` record and every process produces exactly one `session` record, from one wrapper at the composition root, with no tool handler edited.
steps: In `args.ts`, extract the argv reader out of `parseCliArgs` and add `ParsedCliArgs` + `parseCliArgsAndNames`, leaving `parseCliArgs`'s signature and behaviour untouched.
Add the imports (`createTelemetry`, `nullTelemetry`, `type Telemetry`, `type SessionMode`) and build the single recorder in `main`.
Rewrite `callTool` with the `started`/`envelope`/`parsed`/`supplied`/`errorCode` locals, the clamped `recordedTool`, the intersected supplied names and the `finally` that records the call.

Rewrite `runTool` the same way with `parseCliArgsAndNames`, the exit-code-derived status (`absent` for the no-graph `status` line), and `telemetry.close()` in its `finally`; keep the `--help` path record-free.
Add `telemetry` to `Lifecycle`, close it last in `shutdown`, and thread the parameter through `runMcp`, `workerOptions` and `main`'s `try/finally`.
Run `$HOME/.bun/bin/bun test tests/cli.test.ts tests/cli-args.test.ts tests/mcp-surface.test.ts`, then typecheck and lint.
details.verify: `$HOME/.bun/bin/bun run typecheck`, `$HOME/.bun/bin/bun run lint` and `$HOME/.bun/bin/bun test tests/cli.test.ts tests/cli-args.test.ts tests/mcp-surface.test.ts` all pass with 0 failures, and `tests/cli-args.test.ts` does so **unmodified**. Done when all are green, `git status --porcelain` lists no path outside `src/index.ts` and `src/shared/cli/args.ts` (phase_0's files are still uncommitted and expected — no commit happens between tasks), and `grep -rn "process.env" src/` still reports the same four baseline files with no new one (`src/shared/config.ts`, `src/index.ts`, `src/indexer/watch.ts`, `src/tools/index/handler.ts`).

tasks.title: Record calls and the session record at the composition root

details.contract:
`src/indexer/worker.ts` is the only file this task changes. It imports `#shared/telemetry/telemetry` (`nullTelemetry`, `type Telemetry`) and `#shared/telemetry/record` (the spec types). Phase_0's `Telemetry` interface and `IndexRunSpec` already exist.

1. `WorkerOptions` gains `readonly telemetry?: Telemetry;`. `runWorker` uses `const telemetry = options.telemetry ?? nullTelemetry()`, so a direct `runWorker` call (every existing worker test) writes nothing.
2. `RunContext` gains a mutable summary collector, `readonly summary: RunSummary`, with exactly these fields: `filesSeen`, `filesIndexed`, `filesSkipped`, `filesFailed`, `nodesByKind: Record<string, number>`, `edgesByKindTier: Record<string, number>`, `unresolvedCount`, `languages: Record<string, number>`, `filesChangedInRun`. It starts as zeros and empty objects.
3. `indexGraph` fills it where `discovered`, `plan`, `parsed`, `units` and `resolved` are all in scope (between the `bind(...)` call and `withStage`, immediately before `durationMs` at line 332): `filesSeen` = `discovered.files.length`; `filesSkipped` = `discovered.skipped`; `filesIndexed` = parsed entries whose `unit !== null`; `filesFailed` = parsed entries with `parseStatus === "failed"`; `nodesByKind` = `units.flatMap(u => u.nodes)` grouped by `node.kind`; `edgesByKindTier` = `resolved.edges` grouped by `` `${kind}:${tier}` ``; `unresolvedCount` = `units.flatMap(u => u.unresolved).length + resolved.unresolved.length` (the count `persistUnit` writes); `languages` = `discovered.files` grouped by `file.lang` — the field is `lang: LangId` (`src/indexer/discover.ts:43`), not `language`; `filesChangedInRun` = `plan.changed.length`. The `plan.nothingToDo` branch fills only `filesSeen`, `filesSkipped`, `languages` and `filesChangedInRun`, then returns `WORKER_EXIT.nothingToDo`.
4. `runWorker` keeps its control flow and becomes return-at-the-end: hoist `let exitCode: number = WORKER_EXIT.failed`, `let mode: WorkerMode = options.mode ?? "full"` and `let force = options.force === true` above the `try`. The hoisted initializers are **only** the values the early-exit paths report (`WORKER_EXIT.locked` at `:218`, a throw out of `migrateLive`, the `catch`), because those return before the resolution runs. The resolution stays where it is and assigns to the hoisted variables: `force = options.force === true || migrated.rebuildRequired;` and `mode = options.mode ?? (force ? "full" : "fast");` replace the two `const` declarations at `src/indexer/worker.ts:226-227`, so the `mode` handed to `indexGraph` at `:233` is still that resolved value and a default run on a changed tree still indexes `fast`. Never shadow `mode` inside the `try` (a second `const mode` leaves the `finally` reporting `"full"`) and never pass the hoisted initializer to `indexGraph` (that would turn every default run into a full rebuild). The `return` statements inside the `try` become `exitCode = …` assignments, the `catch` keeps `recordFailure` and assigns `WORKER_EXIT.failed`; the `finally` keeps the heartbeat clear and the lock release, then records and closes:

telemetry.recordIndexRun({ mode, exitCode, durationMs: Date.now() - startedAt, wasForced: force, filesSeen: summary.filesSeen, filesIndexed: summary.filesIndexed, filesSkipped: summary.filesSkipped, filesFailed: summary.filesFailed, nodesByKind: summary.nodesByKind, edgesByKindTier: summary.edgesByKindTier, unresolvedCount: summary.unresolvedCount, languages: summary.languages, dbSizeBytes, filesChangedInRun: summary.filesChangedInRun });
telemetry.close();

`dbSizeBytes` is `statSync(livePath).size` in a try/catch returning 0; add `statSync` to the existing `node:fs`/`node:fs/promises` import list. Then `return exitCode;` after the `try/finally` block.
5. `generation_advanced` is derived by `record.ts`, not here: it is `exitCode === WORKER_EXIT.published`. Do not invent a second flag. `v: 1` comes from the builder too; this task passes no version field.

Do not change any log line, any exit code value, the lock protocol, the publish protocol, or the behaviour of a run that finds nothing to do.
details.goal: Every index worker run emits exactly one `index_run` record from the run's single exit path, with counters the worker already computed in memory, and writes nothing when no recorder was supplied.
steps: Add the two imports and `telemetry?: Telemetry` to `WorkerOptions`; resolve `nullTelemetry()` as the fallback.
Add `RunSummary` and the summary collector to `RunContext` with zeroed initial values.
Fill the collector in `indexGraph` from `discovered`, `plan`, `parsed`, `units` and `resolved`, and in the `nothingToDo` branch with the four facts it has.
Hoist `exitCode`, `mode` and `force`, then convert the inner `return`s and the `catch` into `exitCode` assignments.
In the `finally`: heartbeat clear and lock release first, then `recordIndexRun(...)` with `dbSizeBytes` from a guarded `statSync`, then `telemetry.close()`, then `return exitCode` after the block.
Run typecheck, lint and `tests/worker.test.ts`, which must pass untouched.
details.verify: `$HOME/.bun/bin/bun run typecheck`, `$HOME/.bun/bin/bun run lint` and `$HOME/.bun/bin/bun test tests/worker.test.ts tests/index-integration.test.ts` all pass with 0 failures. Done when all three are green, `git status --porcelain` lists no path outside `src/indexer/worker.ts` and the two files TASK-008 changed in this same tree (no commit happens between tasks), and no `process.env` read was added (`grep -n "process.env" src/indexer/worker.ts` prints nothing).

tasks.title: Record one index_run at the worker's single exit path

details.contract:
Create `tests/telemetry-root.test.ts` with `bun:test`. It spawns the shipped entry (`join(APP_ROOT, "bin", "sangkar.ts")`) with `process.execPath` + `"run"`, a 120 s timeout per spawn (a cold index loads tree-sitter grammars), `SANGKAR_NO_WATCH: "1"`, and a `mkdtemp` tree removed in `afterAll`. It never imports `runWorker` or a handler: the point is the executable path. The MCP case speaks JSON-RPC to a spawned server by hand, the way `tests/mcp-surface.test.ts:35-48` does — no SDK client, no import of the server's registry.

Case A (telemetry on, variable unset): in one temp tree run `sangkar index --repo-root <repo> --data-dir <data>`, then `sangkar status --repo-root <repo> --data-dir <data>`. Read every `<data>/telemetry/*.jsonl` line and parse it. Assert: at least one `session` record with `session_mode: "worker"` and one with `"cli"`; exactly one `index_run` with `mode: "full"`, `exit_code: 0`, `generation_advanced: true`, `files_seen >= 1`, `files_indexed >= 1`, a non-empty `languages` object, and `db_size_bytes > 0`; exactly one `call` record with `tool: "status"`, `status: "ok"`, `arg_names_set: []`, `seq === 1`; every record carries `v: 1` and a 32-hex-character `install_id` and `session_id`, and the `session`/`call` pair from one process shares one `session_id`.

Case A2 (supplied names are explicit-only): in the same tree run `sangkar trace handleRequest --depth 1 --repo-root <repo> --data-dir <data>`. Assert the new `call` record has `tool: "trace"` and `arg_names_set` exactly `["depth", "query"]`. Name the mapping in a comment: the bare token `handleRequest` is positional and lands in `query` (`positionalFieldOf`, `src/shared/cli/args.ts:132-137`, consumed by the positional branch at 240-244), and `--depth 1` is a flag. `cursor` and `budget` must be absent from the set even though the manifest declares both, and `budget_tokens` must be the effective `3200` — a defaulted name is not a supplied name, while the budget in force is the defaulted value.

Case A3 (a default run stays `fast`) — recommended and worth its one extra spawn, because TASK-009 hoists `mode` and the cheap way to get that wrong is to let the hoisted initializer reach `indexGraph`: in a second temp tree, index once (that run records `mode: "full"`), append one line to an indexed source file so the tree changes, then index again. Assert the second `index_run` record has `mode: "fast"` and `was_forced: false`, matching the worker's own resolution at `src/indexer/worker.ts:226-227`. No new fixture and no new helper: the same tree, one more spawn.

Case B (telemetry off): a second temp data dir; spawn `sangkar status` with `SANGKAR_TELEMETRY: "off"`; assert `<dataB>/telemetry` does not exist after the child exits 0.

Case C (privacy at the boundary): concatenate the JSONL text from case A and assert the temp repo path does not appear in it, proving `--repo-root` never reaches a record.

Case D (a client-supplied tool name is not recorded): spawn `sangkar mcp --repo-root <repo> --data-dir <data>`, hand-write the three frames (`initialize`, `notifications/initialized`, then `tools/call` with `params.name` set to a path-shaped string such as `"/tmp/<fixture>/secret.ts"` and empty arguments), close stdin, and wait for exit. Assert exactly one `call` record with `tool: "unknown"`, and that no line of the JSONL contains `secret.ts` or the fixture path — the string is not an argument and must not survive as a tool name.

Case E (a successful process is not an error): a third temp data dir with no graph; `sangkar status` there writes the human no-graph line, exits 0, and records exactly one `call` with `tool: "status"`, `status: "absent"`, `payload_tokens: 0`, `truncated: false`. The record's status and the exit code must agree; `"error"` here would label the commonest CLI invocation a failure.

Do not assert on log wording, on the file name beyond its `YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl` shape, or on the count of `session` records beyond "at least one per mode". Do not weaken any case.
details.goal: The wiring is proven through the shipped command in a real temp tree: an indexed tree yields one index_run plus cli call records, and the off switch leaves no telemetry directory behind.
steps: Create the file with a spawn helper that deletes every inherited `SANGKAR_*` key and then sets what each case needs, a 120 s budget per spawn, and the temp trees removed in `afterAll`.
Case A: index then status in one temp tree; assert the record kinds, the `index_run` counters, `arg_names_set: []` and the shared `session_id` and `v: 1`.
Case A2: `trace handleRequest --depth 1` and assert `["depth", "query"]` with no `cursor`/`budget` and `budget_tokens: 3200`.

Case A3: a second, default index after one source edit records `mode: "fast"` with `was_forced: false`. Cases B and E: `SANGKAR_TELEMETRY=off` creates no `telemetry/` directory; a data dir with no graph yields one `call` with `status: "absent"` beside an exit code of 0.
Case C and D: the temp repo path appears in no line; the MCP `tools/call` with a path-shaped name records `tool: "unknown"` with none of that string in the file.
Run the file alone, then the full suite.
details.verify: `$HOME/.bun/bin/bun test tests/telemetry-root.test.ts` passes with 0 failures and at least 6 tests, then `$HOME/.bun/bin/bun test` passes overall with 0 failures. Done when both are green and `git status --porcelain` lists no path outside `tests/telemetry-root.test.ts` and phase_1's two instrumented files (still uncommitted and expected — no commit happens between tasks).

tasks.title: End-to-end proof that a real run writes real records

details.contract: Read-only. Do not edit any file. Compare `git status --porcelain` against the phase's owned paths and report a deviation instead of fixing it.
details.goal: Prove the instrumented product still passes everything it passed before, with the boundary rules and stdout discipline intact.
steps: Run `$HOME/.bun/bin/bun run typecheck` and `$HOME/.bun/bin/bun run lint`.
Run `$HOME/.bun/bin/bun run db:drift` and confirm no migration file changed.
Run the full suite `$HOME/.bun/bin/bun test` and record pass/fail counts; `tests/publish.test.ts`, `tests/smoke.test.ts` and `tests/worker.test.ts` must be green and unmodified.
Confirm `tests/boundary.test.ts` is unmodified and `git diff --name-only HEAD -- src/tools` is empty.
Confirm `git status --porcelain` lists, for this phase, only `src/index.ts`, `src/shared/cli/args.ts`, `src/indexer/worker.ts` and `tests/telemetry-root.test.ts`.
Record every result in `ppm task_write_progress`.
details.verify: Done when typecheck, lint, db:drift and the full suite exit 0, `src/tools/**` is untouched, and the phase's changed-file list matches exactly — including `src/shared/cli/args.ts`, whose one additive export is this phase's only change outside the two instrumented files. A red test is reported with its name and diff, never silenced.
